targetText: The metaphysical or vulgar evolutionist world outlook sees things as isolated, static and one-sided.
explanation: Metaphysical thinking assumes things stay fixed and act independently. For example, treating a failing student as simply 'lazy' ignores their health, study environment, and home life, reducing a complex person to a single fixed trait.

targetText: It holds that external causes are the condition of change and internal causes are the basis of change, and that external causes become operative through internal causes.
explanation: Outside events can trigger changes, but what actually happens depends on what is inside. Real-life example: Boiling water softens a carrot but hardens an egg. The outside heat is the same, but the internal nature of the object determines the result.

targetText: In a suitable temperature an egg changes into a chicken, but no temperature can change a stone into a chicken, because each has a different basis.
explanation: Mao uses this biological analogy to show that outside effort only produces results if the internal foundation is ready. Real-life example: Giving world-class sports coaching to a trained athlete can create a champion, but giving that same coaching to a wooden chair will never make it run.
